Phainon watches him go, his expression unreadable. But when Mydei looks at him, Phainon meets his gaze and smiles- soft, triumphant, unwavering.

And Mydei, still lost in the depths of a conversation he doesn't fully understand, can only nod in return.

The room is still. Silent, save for the soft, steady rhythm of his breathing and the gentle wind that brushes against the stone of the window. Mydei is awake, though his body still feels foreign to him, a lingering fatigue pressing against his chest as he pushes himself to sit up. This is new, even after his deaths his symptoms did not last for such a long time. His head is heavy, his thoughts clouded with the aftershocks of everything that has happened, and yet a strange pull drags his attention to the window.

His gaze drifts toward the source of the subtle change, toward the dark expanse of the sky. For the first time in what feels like a lifetime, Mydei’s eyes meet the night, real night.

“Today is the first time it actually became night.” Phainon talks quietly by his side, once he notices where Mydei’s attention shifted.

“So far, it only grew darker each day, never truly becoming night. It seems like you waking up brought back the balance to Amphoreus.” He speaks as if he is letting Mydei in on a secret, a mischievous smile on his face that softens once he notices the blonde Prince not paying attention to him. He watches him, as Mydei watches the sky.

It’s impossible to explain, but the absence of Kephale’s sun is a profound void. There’s a chill to the air now, an unfamiliar coolness that hasn’t touched this land in eons. The constant day that Kephale’s sun had provided is gone, leaving the world draped in something quiet, something vast.

Mydei watches the stars.

Stars.

They are small and cold, scattered across the ink-black sky like fragments of a broken mirror. His heart trembles at their cold beauty. He doesn’t remember the last time he saw them, but they feel like a distant memory, like something that belongs to another life.

He feels something tug inside him, a quiet ache that pulls at his chest, deeper than the emotional wounds that still have yet to heal. The vastness of the sky stretches on before him, and in that endless space, something feels lost, something he can’t quite name.

Mydei’s lips part, his breath a soft whisper as his gaze drifts down to the dark expanse. It’s all he’s ever known, that eternal daylight. The sun that never sets. But now... now, it is gone, and all that remains is this vast, empty sky.

“I’ve never seen it like this before,” Mydei says quietly, his voice still raw, as if waking from a long, unsettling dream. “The stars. It feels... strange. Like the world has changed.”

Phainon is silent for a moment, his gaze following Mydei’s to the sky. Mydei can feel the weight of the silence, heavy with an emotion Phainon doesn’t voice.

“It is strange.” Phainon agrees, his voice soft. “The world is changing, Mydei. Kephale’s sun is no longer here, and with it, the tide of chaos that followed it. We can rest now. You can let your responsibilities go. It is done now.”

Mydei’s chest tightens, and a wave of confusion washes over him. He stares at the stars as if they might hold the answers, as if somehow their cold, distant light can explain the emptiness he feels inside himself.

“There’s nothing left for me to hold on to.” Mydei whispers, almost to himself. The silence presses in around him.  It feels like he is telling Phainon his deepest, darkest secret, one that he will regret once his right mind comes back and Mydei isn’t tired. The night feels like an old wound, reopened. For so long, the sky had been a constant, a source of warmth, of light. Now, it is void, empty of everything but the cold.

“Hold on to me, Mydei. I will give you a new reason to live for.” Phainon says softly, his voice gentle but laden with something Mydei can’t quite place. He reaches out, fingers touches Mydei’s bare hands, sending shivers down his spine.

Mydei looks down at his hands, fingers trembling as they rest on the blanket, Phainon’s hand enveloping his own. He feels... adrift. Like a part of him has been severed, torn away, and he doesn’t know how to make sense of it. How to make sense of this new life.

Phainon shifts beside him, and Mydei can feel his presence- solid, warm, steady. Yet it doesn’t settle the storm inside him.

“You’ve never seen it like this, Mydei.” Phainon says again, his voice thick with unspoken emotion as his eyes shift back to the vastness of the night sky. “You’ve never seen the sky without the sun.”

Mydei takes a deep breath, trying to steady himself, but the weight of everything pressing on him feels unbearable. “I don’t know what to make of it. It’s beautiful thought.” he confesses. His voice cracks slightly, and he swallows, his throat tight as his eyes take in the countless glinting stars. “The world is changing, but I feel like I’m stuck. I don’t even know what I’m supposed to do anymore.”

“The world is always changing,” Phainon says, his voice softer now, almost a whisper. “But you’re not alone. Not anymore. We’ll find our way through this, Mydei. I’ll be here.” He repeats his silent promise to him.

Mydei doesn’t respond right away. He doesn’t know how to. Instead, he turns back to the window, his gaze locked on the stars once more. The emptiness of the sky mirrors the emptiness in him, and yet, there’s a strange sort of comfort in that void. It’s raw, unyielding, and it feels like the beginning of something he hasn’t yet come to understand.

For the first time in his life, the night sky is his, so similar to the evernight sky he faced when stepping ashore from the River of Souls. It’s cold, unfamiliar, but it’s his to face.

The night may be endless. But so are their new opportunities.

And for the first time in centuries, feeling afraid of the unknown does not send unease down Mydei’s spine. Not with Phainon by his side.
